references.text: Describes the same event where Jesus withdraws from the Jews after they attempted to stone him, and goes to another city (Ephraim) to be with his disciples.
The immediate context that triggers Jesus' departure to Ephraim; the counsel to kill him meant he could no longer move about publicly.
Marks the end of the stay in Ephraim and the transition to the next event (the raising of Lazarus) before Jesus' final entry into Jerusalem.
